purpose: This medication is used to treat HIV, the virus that can lead to AIDS. It helps reduce the amount of HIV virus in your body and keeps your immune system stronger. It is usually taken along with other HIV medicines as part of a combination treatment plan.
how_it_works: HIV needs to make copies of itself to spread in your body, and it uses special tools called proteases to do this. Lopinavir blocks that tool so the virus cannot make working copies of itself. Ritonavir is added not to fight HIV directly, but to slow down how your body breaks down lopinavir, so it stays in your system longer and works better.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, and feeling tired. Some people notice headaches or a mild rash. Diarrhea is especially common, so staying well hydrated is important.
warnings: This medication can interact with many other medicines, so always tell your doctor and pharmacist about everything you take, including vitamins and herbal supplements. It may affect your heart rhythm, cholesterol, and blood sugar levels, so regular check-ups are important. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, as stopping can make the virus harder to treat.
typical_dosing: For most adults, the usual dose is 2 tablets (each containing 200mg lopinavir and 50mg ritonavir) taken twice a day with or without food. Your doctor may adjust the dose depending on your specific situation and other medicines you take. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly.
